what: The Random Number Generator picks whole numbers at random between a lowest and a highest value that you choose. It can give one number or up to 1,000 at a time, with or without repeats, and can sort them for you.

People use it to pick a winner for a giveaway, draw raffle tickets, choose a student or a team order, play games, pick lottery-style numbers, or create random test data. It is fairer and faster than drawing names from a hat.
The numbers come from your browser’s secure random generator; nothing is sent to a server.
uses: Number your entries from 1 to the total, then generate one number to choose the winner.
Choose which student answers next, or split a class into random groups.
Roll a die with From 1 and To 6, or choose a random number for a board game or quiz.
Get 6 different numbers from 1 to 49 with "No repeats" and "Sort results" ticked.
Pick random IDs or rows to check, or create lists of numbers for testing a spreadsheet.
tutorial: Type the smallest number in "From" and the largest in "To". Both ends are included. Negative numbers work too, for example From -10 To 10. Decimals are rounded to whole numbers.
In "How many numbers", type a count from 1 to 1000. The default is 1.
Tick "No repeats" when each number may appear only once, like drawing tickets from a box. You cannot ask for more numbers than exist in the range; for 1 to 10 the most is 10.
Tick "Sort results" to list the numbers from smallest to largest. Leave it off to keep them in the order they were drawn.
The numbers appear in the big box, separated by commas, for example "14, 3, 27". Click again for a new draw. When the page first opens, one number from 1 to 100 is already shown.
Click "Copy" to copy the list and paste it into a spreadsheet, message or document.
features: Uses the browser’s crypto random source with a method that avoids bias, so every number in the range is equally likely.
Positive or negative, as long as the range covers no more than about 4.29 billion numbers.
Draw one number or a large batch in one click.
Each number appears at most once, like drawing without putting tickets back.
Shows the results from smallest to largest.
Copy the whole list at once.

example.title: Worked example: a lottery-style draw
example.text: You want 6 different numbers between 1 and 49. Type 1 in "From", 49 in "To" and 6 in "How many numbers". Tick "No repeats" and "Sort results", then click "Generate". The box might show "4, 11, 19, 23, 36, 48". Each possible set of 6 is equally likely; there are 13,983,816 different sets, so do not expect to predict a real lottery.

tips: For a giveaway, write down the numbered list of entries before you draw, and share a screen recording of the draw for transparency.
To simulate two dice, generate 2 numbers from 1 to 6 with repeats allowed.
For random groups, number the people, generate all of them with "No repeats", and split the list into groups in that order.
Leave "Sort results" off if the order of drawing matters, for example first, second and third prize.
problems: Swap the two numbers so the smaller one is in "From".
